```{r setup, include = FALSE}
                      dev = "svg")
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
```

# Settings

Edit this chunk to change what counts as detected and what the feasibility
flags warn about. Nothing is excluded anywhere in this report.

```{r settings}
# A locus or family counts as detected at or above this many fragments
detect_min <- 5

# Feasibility flags for locus-level analysis. Warn only.
flag_min_erv_fragments <- 1e5    # total fragments assigned to the annotation
flag_min_loci_detected <- 1000   # loci at or above detect_min

# How a family name is split into the two element classes. The retro.hg38.v1
# annotation combines HERV_rmsk (endogenous retroviruses) with L1Base
# (LINE-1), and the two are reported separately throughout: L1 biology and its
# false-positive modes differ enough that a combined total would be hard to
# interpret.
l1_pattern <- "^L1"

# Number of families to show in the plots
n_top_families <- 15
```

```{r read}
out_step <- file.path(params$out_dir, "03_erv")
counts_dir <- file.path(out_step, "counts")

samples_meta <- read_tsv(params$sample_sheet, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(any_of(c("sample_id", "body_site", "group", "batch")))

if ("body_site" %in% names(samples_meta)) {
  samples_meta <- samples_meta |>
    mutate(body_site = str_to_lower(str_trim(body_site)))
}

locus_counts <- read_tsv(file.path(counts_dir, "erv_counts_locus.tsv"),
                         show_col_types = FALSE)
family_counts <- read_tsv(file.path(counts_dir, "erv_counts_family.tsv"),
                          show_col_types = FALSE)
erv_stats <- read_tsv(file.path(counts_dir, "erv_counts_stats.tsv"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

sample_cols <- setdiff(names(locus_counts), "locus")

# Size factors from module 02, estimated on cellular genes. ERV counts are
# never normalised by ERV counts: a global ERV induction would otherwise be
# divided away by its own normalisation.
size_factor_file <- file.path(params$out_dir, "02_expression", "size_factors.tsv")
have_size_factors <- file.exists(size_factor_file)

if (have_size_factors) {
  size_factors <- read_tsv(size_factor_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    select(sample_id, size_factor)
} else {
  size_factors <- tibble(sample_id = sample_cols, size_factor = NA_real_)
}

is_blank <- function(x) !is.na(x) & str_starts(x, "blank")
```

# Run summary

```{r run_summary}
long_counts <- locus_counts |>
  pivot_longer(-locus, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "count")

per_sample <- long_counts |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  summarise(
    assigned_fragments = sum(count),
    loci_detected      = sum(count >= detect_min),
    loci_nonzero       = sum(count > 0),
    top_locus_share    = if (sum(count) > 0) max(count) / sum(count) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(select(erv_stats, sample_id, any_of("no_feature")), by = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(size_factors, by = "sample_id")

per_sample |>
  transmute(
    sample = sample_id,
    site   = if ("body_site" %in% names(per_sample)) body_site else NA,
    group  = if ("group" %in% names(per_sample)) group else NA,
    `ERV fragments`  = round(assigned_fragments),
    `loci detected`  = loci_detected,
    `loci non-zero`  = loci_nonzero,
    `top locus %`    = round(100 * top_locus_share, 1),
    `size factor`    = round(size_factor, 3)
  ) |>
  kable(caption = paste0("Detected means at or above ", detect_min,
                         " fragments. Size factors come from module 02."))
```

`r if (!have_size_factors) "**Size factors not found.** Normalised values below are omitted; run the module 02 report first."`

The statistics table from Telescope, as written by the pipeline:

```{r telescope_stats}
kable(erv_stats)
```

# HERV and LINE-1

The annotation combines HERV_rmsk.hg38.v2 with L1Base.hg38.v1, so roughly half
its loci are LINE-1 rather than endogenous retroviruses. Both are quantified
together, deliberately: LINE-1 elements are numerous and highly similar to each
other, so removing them from the annotation would push their reads onto HERV
loci during the EM step. They are reported separately from here on.

```{r class_split}
family_long <- family_counts |>
  pivot_longer(-family, names_to = "sample_id", values_to = "count") |>
  mutate(element_class = if_else(str_detect(family, l1_pattern), "LINE-1", "HERV"))

class_summary <- family_long |>
  group_by(sample_id, element_class) |>
  summarise(fragments = sum(count),
            families_detected = sum(count >= detect_min),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id")

class_summary |>
  select(sample_id, any_of(c("body_site", "group")), element_class,
         fragments, families_detected) |>
  mutate(fragments = round(fragments)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = element_class,
              values_from = c(fragments, families_detected)) |>
  kable(caption = "Fragments and families detected, split by element class")
```

```{r class_plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
class_plot_data <- class_summary
if (isTRUE(params$exclude_blanks_from_plots) && "group" %in% names(class_summary)) {
  class_plot_data <- filter(class_summary, !is_blank(group))
}

ggplot(class_plot_data,
       aes(x = sample_id, y = fragments, fill = element_class)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fragments assigned", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

# Detection depth

How many loci carry a usable number of fragments decides whether locus-level
analysis is possible at all. Family-level aggregation is the fallback: fewer
features, more fragments each.

```{r detection_curve, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
thresholds <- c(1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100)

curve_data <- map_dfr(thresholds, function(threshold) {
  long_counts |>
    group_by(sample_id) |>
    summarise(n_loci = sum(count >= threshold), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(threshold = threshold)
}) |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id")

if (isTRUE(params$exclude_blanks_from_plots) && "group" %in% names(curve_data)) {
  curve_data <- filter(curve_data, !is_blank(group))
}

ggplot(curve_data,
       aes(x = threshold, y = n_loci, group = sample_id,
           colour = if ("body_site" %in% names(curve_data)) body_site else NULL)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = thresholds) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(x = "Minimum fragments per locus", y = "Loci detected", colour = "Site") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r detection_table}
curve_data |>
  select(sample_id, threshold, n_loci) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = threshold, values_from = n_loci,
              names_prefix = "at ") |>
  kable(caption = "Loci detected at increasing fragment thresholds")
```

# Dominant loci

Telescope's `final_count` is an expected value under the EM model, so a locus
can accumulate a large count from fragments that align ambiguously to many
places.

`unique_count` is the number of fragments whose alignments all fall inside a
single annotated locus. It is reported here next to the number of loci in that
locus's family, because the two are tightly linked: in a family with hundreds
or thousands of near-identical copies, a fragment from a genuinely transcribed
copy will almost always also align to its siblings and so be classed as
ambiguous. A low unique fraction in a large family is therefore the expected
state and says nothing about data quality; a low unique fraction in a small
family is worth a closer look.

What a high-count, low-unique locus means is that the family is expressed and
the model has had to choose which copy to credit. The family total is on firm
ground; the choice of copy within it is not.

```{r read_full_reports}
telescope_dir <- file.path(out_step, "telescope")

find_report <- function(sample_id) {
  candidates <- c(
    file.path(telescope_dir, sample_id, paste0(sample_id, "-TE_counts.tsv")),
    file.path(telescope_dir, sample_id, paste0(sample_id, "-telescope_report.tsv"))
  )
  existing <- candidates[file.exists(candidates)]
  if (length(existing) > 0) {
    return(existing[1])
  }
  globbed <- Sys.glob(file.path(telescope_dir, sample_id, paste0(sample_id, "-*.tsv")))
  if (length(globbed) > 0) {
    return(globbed[1])
  }
  NA_character_
}

read_report <- function(sample_id) {
  path <- find_report(sample_id)
  if (is.na(path)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  read_tsv(path, comment = "#", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
    mutate(sample_id = sample_id)
}

full_reports <- map_dfr(sample_cols, read_report)

have_full_reports <- nrow(full_reports) > 0 &&
  all(c("transcript", "final_count", "unique_count") %in% names(full_reports))
```

`r if (!have_full_reports) "**Per-sample Telescope reports not found or missing the expected columns.** This section is skipped."`

```{r family_sizes}
# Number of loci per family, taken from the count matrix (Telescope reports
# every annotated locus, so this is the annotation's own copy number)
family_size <- locus_counts |>
  mutate(family = if_else(str_detect(locus, "_"),
                          str_remove(locus, "_[^_]*$"),
                          locus)) |>
  count(family, name = "loci_in_family")
```

```{r dominant_loci, eval = have_full_reports}
locus_detail <- full_reports |>
  filter(transcript != "__no_feature") |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  mutate(share = final_count / sum(final_count)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    unique_fraction = if_else(final_count > 0, unique_count / final_count, NA_real_),
    element_class = if_else(str_detect(transcript, l1_pattern), "LINE-1", "HERV"),
    family = if_else(str_detect(transcript, "_"),
                     str_remove(transcript, "_[^_]*$"),
                     transcript)
  ) |>
  left_join(family_size, by = "family") |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id")

locus_detail |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  slice_max(final_count, n = 3, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  arrange(desc(share)) |>
  transmute(
    sample = sample_id,
    site = if ("body_site" %in% names(locus_detail)) body_site else NA,
    locus = transcript,
    class = element_class,
    final_count = round(final_count),
    `share of sample %` = round(100 * share, 1),
    unique_count = round(unique_count),
    `unique %` = round(100 * unique_fraction, 1),
    `loci in family` = loci_in_family
  ) |>
  kable(caption = paste("Three highest-count loci per sample.",
                        "A low unique % alongside a large family is expected,",
                        "not a warning."))
```

```{r unique_support_plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, eval = have_full_reports}
plot_detail <- locus_detail |>
  filter(final_count >= detect_min)

if (isTRUE(params$exclude_blanks_from_plots) && "group" %in% names(plot_detail)) {
  plot_detail <- filter(plot_detail, !is_blank(group))
}

ggplot(plot_detail,
       aes(x = final_count, y = unique_fraction,
           colour = if ("body_site" %in% names(plot_detail)) body_site else NULL)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "final_count (log scale)",
       y = "Fragments aligning uniquely to this locus",
       colour = "Site") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Loci low on the vertical axis are ones the model had to place among several
candidate copies. Read them together with family size: most will belong to
large families, where that is unavoidable.

```{r unique_support_summary, eval = have_full_reports}
locus_detail |>
  filter(final_count >= detect_min) |>
  group_by(sample_id) |>
  summarise(
    `loci at or above detect_min` = n(),
    `median unique %` = round(100 * median(unique_fraction, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    `low unique, large family` = sum(unique_fraction < 0.10 & loci_in_family >= 100,
                                     na.rm = TRUE),
    `low unique, small family` = sum(unique_fraction < 0.10 & loci_in_family < 100,
                                     na.rm = TRUE),
    `share of signal, low unique %` = round(
      100 * sum(share[unique_fraction < 0.10], na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  kable(caption = paste("Loci the model had to place. The split by family size",
                        "separates the expected cases (large families) from the",
                        "ones worth checking (small families)."))
```

## Concentration within a family

When a family's signal sits almost entirely on one of its copies, that can be
genuine (copies do differ in expression) or it can be the model settling on one
candidate. Comparing across individuals separates the two: a copy that takes
the same large share in every person is more likely to be really expressed,
while a share that jumps between people points at the model choosing.

```{r family_concentration, eval = have_full_reports}
concentration <- locus_detail |>
  filter(loci_in_family >= 10) |>
  group_by(sample_id, family) |>
  summarise(
    family_total = sum(final_count),
    top_locus = transcript[which.max(final_count)],
    top_share = max(final_count) / sum(final_count),
    loci_in_family = first(loci_in_family),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id")

if ("group" %in% names(concentration)) {
  concentration <- filter(concentration, !is_blank(group))
}

concentration |>
  group_by(family) |>
  filter(sum(family_total) > 0) |>
  summarise(
    loci_in_family = first(loci_in_family),
    `total fragments` = round(sum(family_total)),
    `median top-copy share %` = round(100 * median(top_share), 1),
    `same top copy in n samples` = max(table(top_locus)),
    `n samples` = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  slice_max(`total fragments`, n = 15) |>
  kable(caption = paste("Families with 10 or more copies, by total fragments.",
                        "A high top-copy share that falls on the same copy in",
                        "every sample is the more credible pattern."))
```

# Loci analysable within a site

A locus can only enter a locus-level model if it is detected across the
samples being compared. This is the figure the feasibility thresholds should
be set from, rather than per-sample depth: a sample with many detected loci
contributes nothing if they are different loci each time.

With a pilot of one sample per site per individual these numbers are
necessarily small, and they will grow with the cohort. They are reported here
as a lower bound on what locus-level analysis would have to work with.

```{r analysable_set}
site_counts <- long_counts |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id")

if ("group" %in% names(site_counts)) {
  site_counts <- filter(site_counts, !is_blank(group))
}

if ("body_site" %in% names(site_counts)) {
  analysable <- map_dfr(thresholds, function(threshold) {
    site_counts |>
      group_by(body_site, locus) |>
      summarise(
        n_samples = n(),
        n_detected = sum(count >= threshold),
        .groups = "drop_last"
      ) |>
      summarise(
        `in all samples` = sum(n_detected == n_samples),
        `in at least one` = sum(n_detected >= 1),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) |>
      mutate(threshold = threshold)
  })

  analysable |>
    select(body_site, threshold, `in all samples`, `in at least one`) |>
    arrange(body_site, threshold) |>
    kable(caption = "Loci detected in every sample of a site, and in at least one")
} else {
  cat("No body_site column in the sample sheet; cannot compute per-site sets.\n")
}
```

```{r analysable_class}
if ("body_site" %in% names(site_counts)) {
  site_counts |>
    mutate(element_class = if_else(str_detect(locus, l1_pattern), "LINE-1", "HERV")) |>
    group_by(body_site, element_class, locus) |>
    summarise(n_samples = n(), n_detected = sum(count >= detect_min),
              .groups = "drop_last") |>
    summarise(`loci in all samples` = sum(n_detected == n_samples), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = element_class, values_from = `loci in all samples`) |>
    kable(caption = paste0("Consistently detected loci (at or above ", detect_min,
                           " fragments in every sample of the site), by class"))
}
```

# Families

Counts are divided by the module 02 size factors before comparison, so library
depth does not drive the ranking. Within a site only: the sites differ too much
in recoverable transcriptome for a cross-site comparison of these values to
mean anything.

```{r family_normalised}
family_normalised <- family_long |>
  left_join(size_factors, by = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(normalised = if_else(is.na(size_factor), NA_real_, count / size_factor)) |>
  left_join(samples_meta, by = "sample_id")

if (isTRUE(params$exclude_blanks_from_plots) && "group" %in% names(family_normalised)) {
  family_plot_data <- filter(family_normalised, !is_blank(group))
} else {
  family_plot_data <- family_normalised
}

top_families <- family_plot_data |>
  group_by(family) |>
  summarise(total = sum(count), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(total, n = n_top_families) |>
  pull(family)
```

```{r family_heatmap, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5, eval = have_size_factors}
family_plot_data |>
  filter(family %in% top_families) |>
  mutate(family = factor(family, levels = rev(top_families))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = sample_id, y = family, fill = log10(normalised + 1))) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "mako", direction = -1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "log10\n(normalised + 1)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank())
```

```{r family_table}
family_plot_data |>
  filter(family %in% top_families) |>
  mutate(element_class = if_else(str_detect(family, l1_pattern), "LINE-1", "HERV")) |>
  group_by(family, element_class) |>
  summarise(
    total_fragments = round(sum(count)),
    median_per_sample = round(median(count)),
    samples_detected = sum(count >= detect_min),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total_fragments)) |>
  kable(caption = paste0("Top ", n_top_families, " families by total fragments"))
```

# Blank controls

A negative control should carry few ERV fragments. Anything substantial here
points to contamination or index misassignment rather than biology, and belongs
in the module 05 discussion.

```{r blanks}
if ("group" %in% names(per_sample) && any(is_blank(per_sample$group))) {
  per_sample |>
    filter(is_blank(group)) |>
    transmute(sample = sample_id,
              `ERV fragments` = round(assigned_fragments),
              `loci detected` = loci_detected,
              `share of median real sample` = round(
                100 * assigned_fragments /
                  median(per_sample$assigned_fragments[!is_blank(per_sample$group)]), 2)) |>
    kable()
} else {
  cat("No blank controls in the sample sheet.\n")
}
```

# Feasibility flags

Warnings only. No sample is excluded here or anywhere else in the pipeline.

```{r flags}
flags <- per_sample |>
  mutate(
    flag_fragments = if_else(assigned_fragments < flag_min_erv_fragments,
                             "WARN", "PASS"),
    flag_loci = if_else(loci_detected < flag_min_loci_detected, "WARN", "PASS"),
    locus_level = if_else(flag_fragments == "PASS" & flag_loci == "PASS",
                          "locus level feasible",
                          "family level recommended")
  )

if ("group" %in% names(flags)) {
  flags <- flags |>
    mutate(locus_level = if_else(is_blank(group),
                                 "blank control, not assessed", locus_level))
}

flags |>
  transmute(
    sample = sample_id,
    site = if ("body_site" %in% names(flags)) body_site else NA,
    `ERV fragments` = flag_fragments,
    `loci detected` = flag_loci,
    verdict = locus_level
  ) |>
  kable()

tibble(
  Flag = c("ERV fragments", "Loci detected"),
  Threshold = c(paste("below", format(flag_min_erv_fragments, scientific = FALSE)),
                paste("below", flag_min_loci_detected,
                      "loci at", detect_min, "or more fragments"))
) |>
  kable(caption = "Thresholds in force for this report")
```

# Notes

- Counts are Telescope `final_count`, the column intended for negative-binomial
  models such as DESeq2.
- Normalisation uses module 02 size factors, estimated on cellular genes within
  each body site. ERV counts are never used to normalise themselves.
- Telescope reassigns ambiguously mapped fragments probabilistically rather
  than discarding them, so a locus-level count is an expected value under the
  model, not a count of unambiguous reads. The `unique_count` column of each
  per-sample report gives the unambiguous subset if a locus needs checking.
- The alignment feeding this module is deliberately permissive (bowtie2
  `-k 100`, approximately 95% identity), which is what gives the EM model
  something to work with. It is not comparable to the module 01 STAR alignment.
- LINE-1 and HERV are kept apart throughout. The LINE-1 component is present so
  that its reads are not forced onto HERV loci, not because it is part of the
  study question. Note that LINE-1 resolves to very few families, so
  family-level aggregation is not meaningful on that side; LINE-1 is
  interpretable only at locus level, which is also the least robust level.
- `unique_count` counts fragments whose alignments all fall inside one
  annotated locus. It is confounded with family copy number: in a family of
  hundreds of near-identical copies, almost no fragment can qualify, however
  real the expression. It is reported next to family size for that reason, and
  should not be used as a quality filter on its own, since doing so would
  discard the high-copy families the study is about.
- Family totals are better supported than any individual copy within a family.
  Where a family is large and ambiguity is high, the family-level matrix is the
  defensible unit of analysis and locus-level results are exploratory.
